I like the idea of an open world Pokemon game, BUT I don't think that a good one could come from any of the companies you mention, since they all suffer from the same basic problem - they're no longer designing cutting edge games - they're just churning out profitable content.

In fact, Gamefreak was something of an exception for quite some time, since they were one of the few companies with a successful franchise that was still continuing to improve overall, instead of falling into jettisoning interesting content in favor of shiny graphics and dumb gimmicks in pursuit of broad but shallow appeal. But that ended with gen 5 - since then, they've done the same thing that other companies already did (and Beth - the makers of Skyrim - are a stellar example) - they just churn out superficially impressive but ultimately bland and uninspiring content.

If a truly worthwhile open world Pokemon game were to ever come to be, it would have to be made by a new, upstart company driven by passion, rather than by an old stalwart driven by a corporate bottom-line, and since Gamefreak certainly isn't going to let go of their still-profitable franchise, that isn't going to happen. If the companies you cite really did come together to make such a game, it's guaranteed that it would be a bland, shallow, ultimately uninspiring disappointment, because that's really all that enormous corporate monoliths like that can or will make.

Sorry. It's a great idea, but I just don't see it happening at all, and considering the quality of the games those companies are producing lately, I count that as a good thing. I would tend to think that a game at least something like you envision will happen, but again, it'll come from some new, upstart company driven by passion, so it'll be something other than Pokemon.
